items.title: EAR: Entity-Aware Partitioning Approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Development
items.title_zh: EAR：面向检索增强生成开发的实体感知划分方法
items.summary: EAR is an entity-aware partitioning approach for retrieval-augmented multiple-choice QA that extracts normalized surface anchors from the question, answer options and corpus, then retrieves local windows around matching anchors and can attach a larger parent passage via an extractive summary. On a cleaned 153-question MMLU-style subset with Mistral, Gemma and DeepSeek, entity-window retrieval cut retrieved words by 37.5-40.2% relative to chunks, while accuracy changes were mixed and not statistically significant.

items.title: Amortized Low-Rank Adaptation for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 面向基于模型强化学习的摊销低秩适配
items.summary: CLAW uses a hypernetwork to generate low-rank (LoRA) adapters at test time, so a pretrained world model can adapt to an unknown environment from a small batch of transitions while the base model stays frozen. In locomotion and manipulation environment families, it is reported to outperform gradient-based adaptation and in-context learning using only seconds of test-time data, and to avoid overfitting in data-scarce regimes.

items.title: Adaptive Chemotherapy Control under Tumor Heterogeneity via Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 肿瘤异质性下的自适应化疗控制：一种强化学习方法
items.summary: The study trains continuous (TD3) and discrete (DQN) deep reinforcement learning dosing policies on a high-dimensional heterogeneous tumor model and benchmarks them against a Pontryagin's Maximum Principle open-loop controller. Across a 100-patient virtual cohort with plus or minus 10 percent perturbations in growth and drug-sensitivity parameters, TD3 achieved higher average tumor reduction while DQN gave tighter inter-patient dosing consistency; the simulations assume full observation of all tumor subpopulations.

items.title: GTA: Graph Theory Agent and Benchmark for Algorithmic Graph Reasoning with LLMs
items.title_zh: GTA：面向 LLM 算法图推理的图论智能体与基准
items.summary: The authors introduce GT Bench, a benchmark of 24 classical graph problems in 44 task-structure settings with over 100,000 examples across four input representations, and find that LLM accuracy is strongly tied to representation and shifts with graph density, size and topology. They also propose GTA, which pairs a preference-trained representation selector with plan-and-decompose scaffolding around a frozen executor LLM, lifting Phi-4 from 53.5% to 69.1% on the easy split and from 33.0% to 41.5% on the hard split.

items.title: Learning Symbolic Constraint Representations from Examples: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach
items.title_zh: 从样例中学习符号约束表示：一种神经符号方法
items.summary: The paper proposes a neuro-symbolic framework for automatic constraint acquisition in which learned Oracle Transformer models emulate user responses and interact with the FastCA engine, which refines those responses into a sound, consistent and interpretable constraint network. The authors report that this interplay recovers structured symbolic models from data without prior domain knowledge.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning over Patient Trajectories for Clinical Reasoning in EHR Foundation Models
items.title_zh: 面向 EHR 基础模型临床推理的患者轨迹强化学习
items.summary: The authors propose an RL fine-tuning framework that treats EHR foundation models as generative policies over patient trajectories, formulating clinical prediction problems such as hospital readmission as event-conditioned, time-windowed reasoning tasks with time-aware, rollout-sensitive rewards. They report consistent gains over pretrained backbones and strong baselines, with smaller models surpassing larger pretrained ones in data-limited regimes and positive transfer across tasks.
